focus: Close-out: UX and extension — root cause of the AI_SESSION_CHILD relaunch-suite failure, operator enable-relaunch/brief/history UX, and three extension proposals

graphEvents.label: What blocks the operator or AI user when enabling relaunch, reading the advisor brief or recovering history
Ambient AI_SESSION_CHILD silences the relaunch nudge suites (27/65 and 28/813)
Enable-relaunch recipe has no single owner and its flags file is absent in a fresh clone
No shared cross-runtime detector corpus, so env-isolation gaps go unseen

label: The relaunch nudge is silently off for any test process that inherits AI_SESSION_CHILD. nudgeDecision returns quiet('child-session') at nudge.cjs:569 via a deferred require of goal-core's relaunchSessionIsChild (nudge.cjs:568); the OpenCode plugin passes process.env (session-relaunch.js:183); the shared hermetic fixture drops only relaunch/goal switch keys and HOOK_FLAGS_CONFIG (relaunch-env.cjs HERMETIC_DROP_KEYS), and the suite's ENV_KEYS (session-relaunch.test.cjs:37-53) never names the marker. Measured: env -u AI_SESSION_CHILD -> 65/65 pass; AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 -> 38 pass / 27 fail; the same marker breaks .skilled/hooks/session-relaunch/tests (785/813) while the goal suites stay green because they isolate it themselves (goal-pi.test.mjs:36,40). Fix (reported only): add AI_SESSION_CHILD to HERMETIC_DROP_KEYS and to ENV_KEYS in the plugin suite; suites needing the child path set it explicitly per case. Verify: AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 node --test .opencode/plugins/tests/session-relaunch.test.cjs

The child-session predicate belongs to the goal concern and is loaded lazily from the nudge path: session-relaunch cannot answer 'am I a child' without goal's core, and hides the dependency behind a require inside nudgeDecision's body (nudge.cjs:568), which states a module cycle that was worked around rather than removed. If goal-core.cjs moves or is renamed, relaunch fails at nudge time inside a host callback, not at load. The marker is a shared-contract object and belongs in .skilled/hooks/shared/ beside hook-flags.cjs. Verify: grep -n relaunchSessionIsChild .skilled/hooks/session-relaunch/lib/*.cjs .skilled/hooks/shared/*.cjs -> exactly one hit, the deferred require

The enable-relaunch recipe has no single owner and step 1 targets a file absent from a fresh clone (git ls-files .skilled/hooks/hook-flags.env -> 0 lines, working copy has 5645 bytes). Documented and correct: the enable flags and precedence (ENV-REFERENCE.md:107-109), the four tuning switches with defaults (:119-122), the copy step (hooks/README.md:83, README.md:1604). Wrong doc placement: the relaunch doc says 'Set SYSTEM_SESSION_RELAUNCH_ENABLED=1 in .skilled/hooks/hook-flags.env' (session-relaunch/README.md:89) without the copy step an operator needs first. No doc: the loop requirement — outside skilled-loop a flag-only install produces zero hops until someone asks for /speckit:handoff and runs the printed claim command (README:58); and no doc names the history subcommand as the smoke test that the loop is live (README:122). Half a doc: the doctor can create the file and set one switch (doctor-env.yaml:122) but never says relaunch ships off, so STATUS=OK reads as 'relaunch works'

In the operator-facing docs opened this iteration the advisor appears only as a kill switch: the sole mention is the SYSTEM_SKILL_ADVISOR_DISABLED=0 re-enable example inside the hooks README config paragraph (hooks/README.md:80). No brief-reading or 'why was this skill recommended' recipe appears in the hooks README config section, the ENV-REFERENCE relaunch rows, or the doctor env assets — where relaunch has nine rows with defaults, effects and readers and the advisor has no equivalent block. Scoped: absence in the documents opened, not proof of absence; system-skill-advisor/SKILL.md and hooks/skill-advisor-hook.md were not opened. Verify: grep -n 'SKILL_ADVISOR' .skilled/hooks/README.md .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/ENV-REFERENCE.md

Extension: generate per-runtime adapters and READMEs from one hook manifest. Today one concern carries a directory per runtime with its own adapter and a README whose paragraphs are byte-identical across runtimes (git-worktree-guard claude/codex/cursor/devin README.md:19); the resolver centralizes the names (RUNTIMES, runtimeEnableFlag, DEFAULT_OFF in hooks/shared/hook-flags.cjs) but nothing centralizes the files. Proposal: .skilled/hooks/hooks.manifest.json mapping concern -> runtimes -> adapter entry, event and flag key, with a generator and a tree-matches-manifest test. What breaks today without it: a new runtime is an N-file hand edit per concern with no partial-application detection; the four identical README paragraphs stay in sync only because nobody has edited one. Verify: find .skilled/hooks -maxdepth 3 -name README.md | wc -l

Extension: one shared detector corpus across runtimes, executed twice per case under a clean and a hostile ambient env. Today each runtime has its own adapter and its own test file (ask-surface-guard/dsh/ask-surface-guard.mjs:30, tests/dsh-ask-surface-guard.test.mjs:65) with no shared corpus and no shared ambient-env contract. What breaks today without it: exactly f-iter010-001 — a whole suite's env isolation gap survived the release line because no harness asserts that every runtime's suite behaves the same under a dispatched-child environment; the same shape recurs for every marker the hooks read (AI_SESSION_CHILD, SKILLED_LOOP_*, the six per-runtime switches), and each suite decides for itself what to clear. Proposal: .skilled/hooks/shared/tests/corpus/ plus a per-runtime runner; a case that passes only in the clean run is a finding, not a flake. Verify: AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 node --test .skilled/hooks/session-relaunch/tests/ -> 28 failures today

Extension: drive the doctor's concern report from the flag resolver. The doctor can already create hook-flags.env from the example after an explicit yes and set one eligible non-secret switch (doctor-env.yaml:22,122,140), but DEFAULT_OFF['session-relaunch'] lives only in the resolver and reaches no doctor output, so a clean /doctor:env status coexists with relaunch being off and the only signal is a nudge that never arrives — indistinguishable from 'not near the threshold'. Proposal: a flags-derived row set in doctors doctor-env.yaml plus the presentation asset, enumerating each concern with default, effective value, source file or env, and the exact copy-paste enable line for DEFAULT_OFF concerns. Cheapest of the three: the resolver already exports everything the row needs. Verify: node -e "console.log(require('./.skilled/hooks/shared/hook-flags.cjs').DEFAULT_OFF)" then grep -c session-relaunch .skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-env.yaml

The AI_SESSION_CHILD leak is not OpenCode-only: .skilled/hooks/session-relaunch/tests/ loses 28 of 813 cases under the same marker, so the defect is the shared fixture, not one plugin suite. The goal suites (199/199 under the marker) are the counter-example that proves explicit isolation works — they save and delete the variable themselves.

Any hook suite that drives process.env directly must drop every ambient marker the hook under test reads, and restore it afterwards. Relaunch switches, goal switches and HOOK_FLAGS_CONFIG are dropped by the fixture; AI_SESSION_CHILD, SKILLED_LOOP_ID and the master switch are the markers a future concern is most likely to read without adding them to the drop list.

direction: Treat the 27 failures as an OpenCode plugin defect or a nudge-logic regression
reason: Both directions measured: 65/65 pass with the marker unset, 38/65 with it set, and the same marker breaks an unrelated suite (28/813) while suites that isolate it pass. The nudge logic and the plugin are correct; the test harness is what is defective.
